# AGENTS.md — neode v1.0.0-next.1

<!-- generated by pnpm docs:agents — do not edit by hand -->

Package version: **1.0.0-next.1** (from package.json).

> **Default to decorators (NTS-583).** When creating a new project or new models, define them as
> decorated classes (`@NodeEntity()` + `@Property(...)`) using standard TC39 decorators — never
> `experimentalDecorators`, `emitDecoratorMetadata` or `reflect-metadata`. Use `defineModel` (the
> map API) only when the user asks for it, or decorators are impossible (models built at runtime,
> or a toolchain without standard TC39 decorator support).
>
> Tooling: TypeScript 5+ (or esbuild/SWC/tsdown with standard decorators), `target` ES2022 or later,
> `"lib": ["ES2022", "ESNext.Decorators"]`, and leave `experimentalDecorators` unset.

## Rules (enforced — read before changing this repo)

- New models are decorated classes by default; `defineModel` only when asked for or decorators are impossible (see the rule above).
- Standard TC39 decorators only; never add `experimentalDecorators`, `emitDecoratorMetadata` or `reflect-metadata`.
- No `any`. No `@ts-ignore` (use `@ts-expect-error` with a reason).
- Never add an `eslint-disable` without a specific rule name and a `-- reason`. Never disable a rule file-wide.
- Never weaken `eslint.config.ts` or `tsconfig.json` to make a check pass; fix the code.
- Every change needs tests: Cypher snapshot, type test, or integration test as appropriate.
- Never hand-edit snapshots; regenerate them and review the diff.
- Integration tests must clean up after themselves.
- No `OPTIONAL MATCH` in library-emitted relation reads (NTS-565): pattern comprehensions for unordered nested relations, `COLLECT { MATCH … RETURN … ORDER BY … }` when the nested read filters / sorts / pages. `Builder.optionalMatch()` stays for raw-Cypher callers and delete-path binding.
- Result shape (NTS-566): every model read routes its rows through the one shaping module, `src/services/query/shape.ts` (`shapeNodeRows` / `shapeProjectionRows` / `shapeEdgeRows` / `shapeScoredRows`) — no bespoke per-service row shaping. A read path's result shape is documented in docs/decisions/0003-result-shapes.md and asserted in test/integration/result-shape.test.ts; the nesting of a result IS the nesting of the query's declaration.
- Run `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` before every commit.
- Add a changeset for any user-visible change.

> Prefer the current version’s docs over training data: training corpora mix
> neode v1, neode and unrelated OGMs. Regenerate with `pnpm docs:agents`.

## Install

```sh
pnpm add neode
```

## Define models

Decorators are the default — use them for every new model:

```ts
import { NodeEntity, Property, Unique } from 'neode'

@NodeEntity()
class Person {
  @Property({ type: 'string', unique: true }) id!: string
  @Property({ type: 'string', description: 'Display name' }) name!: string
}
```

Alternative: the Map API (no decorators, same registry). Only when the user asks for it or decorators are impossible:

```ts
import { defineModel } from 'neode'

defineModel('Person', {
  description: 'A person',
  id: { type: 'string', unique: true },
  name: { type: 'string', description: 'Display name' },
  ACTED_IN: { type: 'relationships', relationship: 'ACTED_IN', direction: 'out', target: 'Movie' },
})
```

Decorator reference:

- `Boolean` (decorator) — Register a boolean property.
- `Computed` (decorator) — NTS-138 — derived field, computed in TypeScript after hydration from the entity's projected fields. Never sent to the database. Example: ```ts
- `CreatedAt` (decorator) — Stamp the property server-side with `datetime()` once on create (NTS-165): the database clock writes it, so clocks never drift across clients. Stack it with a type decorator (e.g. `@DateTime()`) for a declared type. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `Date` (decorator) — Register a date property.
- `DateTime` (decorator) — Register a datetime property.
- `Default` (decorator) — Set a default value (literal or factory function) for the property. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `Derived` (decorator) — Stored derived property (NTS-569): computed on the write path from the `from` source properties and stored like a hand-set value — the write-time counterpart of `@Computed` (read-time, never stored). TypeScript-side (`compute`) runs against the entity's property record; Cypher-side (`cypher`) is evaluated by the database inside the write statement with `this` bound to the written node after the sources are set. Exactly one of the two is required. A write touching any source recomputes the value unless the derived property itself is explicitly provided. Example: ```ts
- `Duration` (decorator) — Register a duration property.
- `EndNode` (decorator) — On a relationship entity: the property holding the node at the relationship's end.
- `EntityRepository` (decorator) — Register a custom Repository subclass for an entity (TypeORM parity):
- `Expression` (decorator) — NTS-138 — raw Cypher expression projected into the read query: the escape hatch for graph context the projection builder cannot express yet. The expression references the root node as `this`. shortcut: the embedded Relate engine rejects pattern expressions (patterns inside function calls, e.g. `size((this)-[:R]->())`) inside RETURN projections — prefer
- `Filter` (decorator) — Named global filter (NTS-162): declare a named read filter on the model and it applies to every standard read — find / get / all / paginate / search / knn / eager loads / projections / repository reads — composed in one central place in the query services. - Disable per query with `withoutFilters: ['name']` on the read options; each filter is independent. - Parameterise with `withFilterParams({ name: value }, async () => ...)` (request-scoped, async-safe; NTS-575); the `where` fragment references the value as `$name`. `setFilterParams(name, value)` sets a process-wide default that the scope overrides — it is unsafe under concurrent requests. A filter whose `$name` has no value fails closed with a NeodeError. - `where` is a Cypher predicate over the filtered node; `node` names that node (the read root, or the related node inside a filtered relation's pattern comprehension). Label-state filters (labels-as-state, NTS-128) are just label predicates: `where: 'NOT node:Archived'`. - Over relations, the target model's filters render inside the relation's pattern comprehension — a filtered-out target simply doesn't match, so the edge reads as absent and the parent row survives. Never OPTIONAL MATCH. Example — soft delete + tenancy as independent named filters: ```ts
- `Float` (decorator) — Register a float property.
- `Hidden` (decorator) — Hide the property from the returned model. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `Index` (decorator) — Mark the property as indexed. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `InternalId` (decorator) — Project the node's internal id (elementId) into the property — a read-only structural field, not sent on writes.
- `LabelPresent` (decorator) — NTS-137 — label predicate boolean: true when the node has the given label. Example: ```ts
- `LocalDateTime` (decorator) — Register a local datetime property.
- `LocalTime` (decorator) — Register a local time property.
- `NodeEntity` (decorator) — Register the class as a node model: replays the property/relationship registrations queued by its field decorators, and labels the node with the class name (or `config.labels`).
- `Number` (decorator) — Register a numeric (integer or float) property.
- `OnCreateSet` (decorator) — Mark the property as set on create. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `OneToMany` (decorator) — Register a relationship property holding many related entities. Positional form: target entity (lazy reference), relationship type (omitted matches any type — the pattern renders type-less), direction (default BOTH), eager loading, an agent-facing description, per-relationship cascade and a write-time cardinality (NTS-161 — 'many' by default; 'one' / 'zeroOrOne' restrict the relationship to a single edge, a second relate() throwing CardinalityViolationError).
- `OneToOne` (decorator) — Register a relationship property holding one related entity. The target entity (`config.target()`) is required — standard decorators have no design:type reflection to infer it.
- `OnMatchSet` (decorator) — Mark the property as set on match. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `OtherNode` (decorator) — On a relationship entity: the property holding the node at the far end of the relationship — the end node for an outgoing relationship, the start node for an incoming one (the direction-agnostic alternative to

- `Primary` (decorator) — Mark the property as the model's primary key — Repository lookups and save() match nodes on it. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `Property` (decorator) — Register a property with an explicit type and config, e.g. `@Property({ type: 'string', index: true })`. Prefer this over `@String` to avoid shadowing global types.
- `Protected` (decorator) — Mark the property as protected (never returned to the client). Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `Readonly` (decorator) — Mark the property as read only. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `RelatedMany` (decorator) — NTS-135 — eagerly load related entities as a read-only list. Without `fields`, full entities are eagerly loaded (same behaviour as an eager

- `RelationshipCount` (decorator) — NTS-136 — relationship count projected as an inline `COUNT { }` subquery in the read query (TypeORM
- `RelationshipEntity` (decorator) — Register the class as a relationship model: replays the field registrations queued by its property decorators and marks the metamodel entry as a relationship.
- `RelationshipExists` (decorator) — NTS-137 — relationship existence projected as an inline `EXISTS { }` boolean in the read query. `where` uses `node` as the variable convention for the target node. Example: ```ts
- `Required` (decorator) — Mark the property as required. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `SoftDelete` (decorator) — Declarative soft delete (NTS-510): mark the model so delete() stamps a label + deletedAt instead of DETACH DELETE, and every standard read (find / findAll / all / projections / repository reads) filters the label out. Restore with restore(); hard-delete with delete(force). The label defaults to 'Deleted'; the stamp property is `deletedAt` (declared implicitly, server-stamped with datetime()).
- `StartNode` (decorator) — On a relationship entity: the property holding the node at the relationship's start.
- `String` (decorator) — Register a string property.
- `Time` (decorator) — Register a time property.
- `Unique` (decorator) — Mark the property as unique: installSchema() backs it with a uniqueness constraint, and merge() treats races on it as constraint violations. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `UpdatedAt` (decorator) — Stamp the property server-side with `datetime()` on create and on every write (NTS-165): the database clock writes it, so clocks never drift across clients. Stack it with a type decorator (e.g. `@DateTime()`) for a declared type. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `Uuid` (decorator) — Register a UUID property: validated as a UUID string, defaulting to a random UUID v4 on create (an explicit `config.default` wins).
- `Vector` (decorator) — Declare a vector index over the property (NTS-447): `installSchema()` creates the index with the deterministic `vectorIndexName()` naming, `dropSchema()` drops it, and `knn()` searches it. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked with a type decorator.
- `Version` (decorator) — Optimistic locking (NTS-158): mark the property as the model's version — stamped 0 on create, incremented by 1 on every write addressed to the node, and checked with `WHERE n.version = $expected` when the instance carries the version it was hydrated with. A mismatch (the node changed underneath you) throws `OptimisticLockError` — reload the entity and retry. Version is per node only: writes reached through another node's save (nested relationship targets) never bump it. Stack it with a type decorator (e.g. `@Number()`) for a declared type. Merges onto the existing property, so it can be stacked.

Map-API reference (alternative — not the default):

- `defineModel` (function) — Register a model from a map-based schema definition (neode parity), returning the generated virtual class for the model.
- `extendModel` (function) — neode's extend(): register `as` as a clone of the model `name` with `as` added as an extra label and `schema` merged over the original definition.
- `getModelByName` (function) — Get a previously defined model constructor by name
- `getModelsByName` (function) — Get all defined model constructors, keyed by name
- `SchemaDefinition` (interface) — Map-based schema definition for a model (neode parity). Every key except `labels` defines a property or relationship. Property values may be shorthand type names (`age: 'number'`) or full definitions.

### Repositories & transactions

- `Repository` (class) — Active-record style data-access repository for one registered model — constructor-generic over the model CONSTRUCTOR (NTS-563): the `with` load spec of find / findAll is map-checked against the model's `neodeRelationships` phantom static and the returns narrow, the same with() contract as the facade paths (NTS-154) — the TypeORM-parity surface, obtained via `neode.getRepository(Entity)` or the
- `TransactionalService` (class) — The INeode surface scoped to one open transaction: every read/write runs through the TransactionHandle opened by `Neode#beginTransaction` until its commit/rollback, with the facade's model methods (create, merge, relate, …) mirrored inside that scope. The close endpoints are safe to sequence: a second commit() is a no-op and a rollback after a commit does nothing (the managed scopes commit on success), while a commit after a rollback throws.

## Install schema

Create constraints and indexes declared by the models, then query it:

```ts
import Neode from 'neode'

const neode = new Neode(connection)
await neode.installSchema()
```

### Schema management API

- `ApplySchemaDiffOptions` (interface) — Options for applySchemaDrift.
- `applySchemaDrift` (function) — Apply the missing objects of a drift idempotently — every CREATE carries IF NOT EXISTS. Stale objects are only dropped with `dropStale: true` (dropping is destructive: on a shared database "stale" objects may belong to other applications — review the drift first). Mismatched objects are never applied automatically. Each statement is reported with a SchemaResult, following the SchemaService pattern (NTS-450).
- `formatSchemaDrift` (function) — Human-readable multi-line drift report, grouped by action (missing / stale / mismatched), one line per object plus its fix statement. Pure function — no database access (NTS-450).
- `FulltextIndexDefinition` (interface) — A full-text index to keep installed on the database
- `FulltextIndexService` (class) — Installs/drops the given full-text index definitions, following the same result-reporting pattern as SchemaService
- `InspectOptions` (interface) — Which objects count as "declared" for the inspection: pass the full-text/vector index definitions your installSchema call used, so the diff is not polluted by false "extra" entries. The edition is DETECTED from the connection (NTS-598) — EXISTS / property-type constraints are declared only on Enterprise.
- `inspectSchema` (function) — Read the installed schema (SHOW CONSTRAINTS / SHOW INDEXES) and diff it against the declared schema
- `SchemaDiff` (interface) — The declared-vs-installed diff for one schema family (constraints or indexes): the raw object lists plus the names that only appear on one side.
- `schemaDrift` (function) — Structured schema drift (NTS-450): the declared-vs-installed inspection of constraints and every index kind (range/text/fulltext/vector), with the exact fix statement per entry. Cheap and drift-never-throws: drift is data, not an error — failing a CI run on a non-empty diff is the caller's job.
- `SchemaDrift` (interface)
- `SchemaDriftEntry` (interface) — One drifted schema object: what it is, where it lives, and the exact statement(s) that would resolve the drift (NTS-450)
- `SchemaDriftGroup` (interface) — Drift of one schema family (constraints or indexes), grouped by action
- `SchemaInspection` (interface) — The full inspectSchema result: constraint and index diffs against the declared models.
- `SchemaObject` (interface) — One constraint or index as inspected from the database (SHOW CONSTRAINTS / SHOW INDEXES).
- `SchemaResult` (interface)
- `VectorIndexDefinition` (interface) — A vector index to keep installed on the database
- `vectorIndexName` (function)
- `VectorIndexService` (class) — Installs/drops the given vector index definitions, following the same result-reporting pattern as SchemaService

## Query

```ts
const output = await neode.cypher('MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p LIMIT 10')
```

### Querying API

- `AccessMode` (type) — Session routing for a statement: 'READ' (replica-capable) or 'WRITE' (primaries). Where a query path leaves routing open, the facade's defaultRouting (itself defaulting to 'READ') decides; ConnectionProvider#run defaults to 'WRITE'.
- `BatchStatementError` (interface) — A single failed statement within a batch.
- `BoundBuilder` (class) — A Builder bound to an execution scope — the Neode facade or an open transaction (NTS-554): the plain Builder's fluent surface plus the .read() / .write() terminals, which build-and-run through Neode#read / Neode#write (or the TransactionalService mirrors, in-scope). Created by `neode.query()` / `tx.query()` — the standalone Builder never gains implicit execution.
- `Builder` (class) — Fluent Cypher query builder. A statement-based builder: every `match()` / `create()` / `merge()` call starts a new statement segment; where clauses accumulate against the current segment and are flushed into it when the next segment starts or when `build()` is called. All user values are passed as query parameters - the generated query contains only aliases. The one exception is `RawExpression` property values (NTS-460), which render verbatim into patterns; bind the values they reference via `param(name, value)`. Named read filters compose into the chain with `withFilters(model, alias?, options?)` (NTS-614).
- `BulkChunk` (interface) — The result of one chunk: the rows attempted and the hydrated created/merged entities, in row order
- `BulkOptions` (interface)
- `BulkService` (class) — Bulk CREATE and MERGE via UNWIND: one managed write transaction per chunk, one UNWIND statement per transaction, rows validated and reduced to property maps exactly like the single-create / merge paths. Chunks commit SEPARATELY (NTS-597): a failure partway through leaves the earlier chunks committed — bulk writes are not atomic across chunks. Row preparation bounds its embedding-provider calls at MAX_PREPARE_CONCURRENCY in flight.
- `clearFilterParams` (function) — Clear every filter param (test hygiene — the store is global).
- `Collection` (class) — An iterable wrapper over an array of entities (parity with neode's Collection): reads like an array, serialises through toJson().
- `ConnectionOptions` (interface) — Options a Neode instance accepts alongside its ConnectionProvider.
- `ConnectionProvider` (interface) — The connection port implemented by every backend.
- `CursorPage` (interface) — Cursor/keyset result — items are returned ascending either way
- `CursorPaginateOptions` (interface) — Keyset/cursor pagination on a temporal (or other comparable) property: paginate(model, filter, { limit, orderBy?, after?, before? })
- `CypherOptions` (interface) — Options for the unified raw query entry, `Neode#cypher`.
- `DeleteOptions` (interface)
- `Direction` (const) — Direction of a relationship pattern. BOTH renders an undirected match pattern (`-[r:TYPE]-`), matching relationships of the type in either direction. Undirected is match-only: Neo4j cannot create a relationship without a direction, so the write paths (relate / create / save) reject BOTH with a descriptive error — set OUTGOING or INCOMING to write (NTS-483). Accepts the legacy case-insensitive 'IN' / 'OUT' / 'BOTH' spellings anywhere a direction is taken.
- `EventType` (const) — Lifecycle events emitted by Neode (facade) and TransactionalService (work performed inside an open transaction). Subscribe with `neode.on(EventType.NODE_CREATED, handler)`, unsubscribe with `neode.off(...)`. Handlers receive the affected value as their only argument: | Event | Emitted by | Payload | |------------------------|-------------------------------------|--------------------| | NODE_CREATED | create(), save() when the merge created the node, createMany() | hydrated entity | | NODE_UPDATED | save() when the merge matched an existing node, update(), the label writes (addLabel / removeLabel / soft delete) | hydrated entity | | NODE_MERGED | mergeOn() (also behind merge(), Repository#upsert and mergeMany()) | hydrated entity | | NODE_DELETED | delete() (hard deletes), deleteAll() | deleted entity | | RELATIONSHIP_CREATED | relate() with forceCreate | GraphRelationship | | RELATIONSHIP_MERGED | relate() (MERGE, the default) | GraphRelationship | | RELATIONSHIP_UPDATED | reserved | — | | RELATIONSHIP_DELETED | reserved (detach) | — | | QUERY_EXECUTED | every statement run through the | QueryExecutedEvent | | | instance's connection (raw + | | | | service queries, inside and outside | | | | transactions) | | Events are emitted synchronously on an EventEmitter scoped to the Neode instance.
- `GraphNode` (interface) — A node value in a normalized shape, as returned in result records.
- `GraphRelationship` (interface) — A relationship value in a normalized shape, as returned in result records.
- `hasProjectedProperties` (function) — True when any property of the model projects a read-model value
- `hydrate` (function) — Hydrate a raw query result (as returned by readCypher/writeCypher or Builder#execute) into typed entities: each record's `alias` column is the node, any other column feeds eager relationship hydration (neode's Factory.hydrate)
- `hydrateFirst` (function) — Hydrate the first record of a raw query result, or undefined when the result set is empty (neode's Factory.hydrateFirst)
- `hydrateProjection` (function) — Hydrate one row of a projection read (NTS-135/136/137/138). The RETURN map projection (projectionNode) carries the node properties inline with the identity markers and eager relationship values — the shape hydrateNode understands, so projected values land on the entity through the regular property hydration switch. This pass then post-processes the projected kinds: - full-entity
- `instrumentConnectionProvider` (function) — Instrument a provider transparently: property reads the wrapper doesn't satisfy — duck-typed introspection such as `connection.database` on the neo4j provider — forward to the inner provider, so consumers holding `Neode#getConnection()` see through the instrumentation.
- `jsonSafe` (function) — JSON-safe serialisation for raw query values: converts the driver class instances that survive value normalisation (Integer, temporal types, Point, Path) and bigints into structures that survive JSON.stringify, recursing through arrays and plain objects. Everything else passes through unchanged.
- `jsonSafeRecord` (function) — A QueryRecord whose values are JSON-safe (the rows of `Neode#cypher`).
- `knn` (function) — k-nearest-neighbour search over a vector index, returning hydrated entities with their similarity score, best match first. With the default `auto` mode the Cypher 25 `SEARCH` clause is attempted first and the queryNodes procedure is used as a fallback; when the backend supports neither a combined error is raised. NTS-162 — the model's named read filters apply to both query forms (a `WHERE` over the matched / YIELDed rows); `filters.withoutFilters` disables names for this call. NTS-584 — the filters are a post-filter over the index's top-k: the SEARCH clause's in-index `WHERE` only takes property predicates over properties registered as additional filter properties on the vector index (which neode's index definitions never declare) and has no label predicates, so the soft-delete filter can never go there. Filtered searches therefore over-fetch round over round until k rows survive the filters or the round cap gives up — k is filled whenever that many valid neighbours exist.
- `KnnMode` (type) — Which query form to use for the kNN search
- `LabelPredicate` (class)
- `LoadedEntity` (type)
- `ManyAndCount` (interface) — Non-paginated `{ items, total }` read (Prisma's findManyAndCount)
- `MAX_CASCADE_DEPTH` (const) — Maximum depth of the self-referential cascade walk — the delete-path counterpart of MAX_TRAVERSE_DEPTH (traverse) and MAX_CREATE_DEPTH (services/write-utilities). Overridable per call with the `depth` option of (NTS-595).
- `Neo4jConnectionProvider` (class) — ConnectionProvider over a neo4j-driver `Driver` (Bolt): Neo4j Community/Enterprise, Aura, Memgraph, or `relate serve`. Result values are normalised out of driver types (Node, Relationship, Integer, temporal, Point) into the plain GraphNode/GraphRelationship shapes; driver errors are mapped through the typed error taxonomy.
- `OffsetPaginateOptions` (interface) — Property -> direction pagination (the classic form): paginate(model, filter, { page, limit, order? })
- `OrderSpec` (type) — Ordering spec, matching neode's all() forms: - `'name'` - order by one property ascending - `['name', 'age']` - order by several properties - `{ name: 'DESC' }` - property -> direction map - `[{ name: 'DESC' }, { age: 'ASC' }]` - list of property -> direction maps - `{ field: 'name', order: 'DESC' }` - two-arg (key, direction) descriptor
- `Page` (interface) — Offset/page result
- `PaginateOptions` (type) — The union of the two pagination modes PaginateService accepts — the options shape (page vs cursor) selects the mode.
- `PaginateService` (class) — Pagination helpers. Two modes, selected by the options shape: - `{ page, limit, order? }` — offset pagination over two autocommit reads (data + COUNT), returning { items, total, page, limit, totalPages } - `{ limit, orderBy?, after?/before? }` — keyset pagination on a temporal property (`WHERE this.createdAt > datetime($cursor)`), returning { items, nextCursor, hasMore }
- `projectionNode` (function) — The RETURN map projection for a model's read query: all properties, the hydration identity markers, full-entity eager relationships and every projected property — one query per read. `withSpec` (NTS-560, NTS-154) additionally renders requested non-eager relationships: `true` renders the standard comprehension fragment, a nested spec object renders the level's spec fragment (the NTS-498 shape, keys validated down the target's declared relationship graph), and a decorating callback renders `key: <key>_loaded` (`[0]` for singular) — the alias the CALL subquery loadSpecCalls() published. Requested keys count as loaded: the hydrated values materialize as own properties through the regular eager hydration path.
- `ProjectionService` (class) — Read service for models with projected properties (NTS-135/136/137/138): the same match / where surface as the plain query services, but the RETURN map projection carries every projected value — related subsets, counts, exists, label predicates, expressions — in one query per read. NTS-145: object values on
- `Property` (class) — A property in a SET clause: `property operator $param` or, inline in a pattern, `property: $param`. With `isRaw`, the value renders verbatim (an inline Cypher expression, NTS-460) instead of a parameter reference.
- `QueryExecutedEvent` (interface) — Payload of QUERY_EXECUTED, emitted once per executed statement.
- `QueryOutput` (interface) — A query result, independent of the underlying client.
- `QueryParams` (type) — A map of Cypher parameter names to values, bound into the statement — values never render into the query text itself.
- `QueryRecord` (interface) — One row of a query result.
- `QuerySummary` (interface) — Metadata for one executed statement: write counters and (when the statement is prefixed with EXPLAIN / PROFILE) the server's plan.
- `RawExpression` (class) — A raw Cypher expression used as an inline pattern property value (NTS-460): rendered verbatim into the pattern — `{ prop: <expression> }` — instead of being bound as a parameter. Variable references (`row.answers`), server-side calls (`datetime()`) and parameter references (`$name`, bound via `Builder#param`) are all legal; the expression must never interpolate data.
- `readFilterFragment` (function) — The raw WHERE fragment for the read paths that write their statements by hand (keyset pagination, full-text search, kNN): the active clauses joined with AND, plus the parameters to merge into the statement's parameters.
- `ReadFilterOptions` (interface) — Per-query filter options, accepted by every filtered read (NTS-162): - `withoutFilters` — disable named filters for this query only; each name is independent (disabling one leaves the others active, EF named-filter model). `softDelete` names the built-in
- `RelateConnectionProvider` (class) — ConnectionProvider over the embedded Relate engine (@relate/relate) — in-process, no Bolt server. The engine is a soft dependency, loaded at construction time; the client shapes are structural so it stays that way.
- `RelationshipEdgeRead` (interface) — One result row of an edge-returning related() read (NTS-499): the hydrated related entity (`node`) alongside the traversed relationship itself (`edge`, the normalized GraphRelationship — type, elementId, endpoints and properties). The seed of the NTS-566 result-shape contract: flat, named, no wrapper classes.
- `Repository` (class) — Active-record style data-access repository for one registered model — constructor-generic over the model CONSTRUCTOR (NTS-563): the `with` load spec of find / findAll is map-checked against the model's `neodeRelationships` phantom static and the returns narrow, the same with() contract as the facade paths (NTS-154) — the TypeORM-parity surface, obtained via `neode.getRepository(Entity)` or the
- `requireRelateClient` (function) — Resolve the Relate client module and native library. The client is not yet published to npm, so it is loaded from disk: 1. `RELATE_CLIENT_PATH` env var, or 2. the sibling `relate` repository checkout (`../relate/clients/javascript`) The native library location is passed through via `RELATE_LIB` (see the Relate client's loader) — detected automatically here when a sibling repository checkout exists.
- `Runner` (interface) — Anything able to run statements in its scope (autocommit or transaction).
- `ScoredEntity` (interface) — A hydrated entity with the relevance score of the index that matched it (full-text search, kNN)
- `search` (function) — Full-text search over a full-text index (`CALL db.index.fulltext.queryNodes`), returning hydrated entities with their relevance score, best match first. The query string is bound as a parameter, so Lucene syntax characters in it are still parsed as such — pass user text through `toFulltextQuery` first. NTS-162 — the model's named read filters apply (a `WHERE` after the YIELD); `filters.withoutFilters` disables names for this call.
- `setFilterParams` (function) — Set the process-wide DEFAULT for the parameter a named filter's `where` references as `$name` (`setFilterParams('tenant', 'acme')` for `where: 'node.tenantId = $tenant'`). Values are bound as query parameters — they never render into the query text. UNSAFE UNDER CONCURRENCY: the value is global to the process, so `setFilterParams('tenant', t); await x; query` lets a concurrent request overwrite it between the set and the read — a cross-tenant leak. Use it only for genuinely process-wide values (single-tenant apps, scripts, tests); for per-request values use `withFilterParams`, whose scope wins over this default.
- `SyncEdgesOptions` (interface) — Options for syncEdges (NTS-161): `properties` is applied to the edges NEWLY related by the sync — common edges are left untouched.
- `SyncEdgesResult` (interface) — What a sync did: how many edges were related and how many detached (zero and zero for a no-op sync — nothing is written)
- `toCollection` (function) — Hydrate a raw query result into a Collection (neode's Factory.hydrate return shape)
- `toDirection` (function) — Normalise a direction given in any supported spelling to a Direction. Unknown values fall back to BOTH (the most permissive direction), matching neode's behaviour of never throwing on a bad direction.
- `toJson` (function) — Convert an entity into a JSON friendly object: plain properties (hidden, protected and structural properties skipped), `_id` (elementId when the model carries an internal id property) and `_labels` (the schema's labels). Eagerly loaded relationships are serialised recursively. `options.relationships` (NTS-564) controls relationship serialisation — `include` / `exclude` name declared relationships, `depth` bounds the levels. Without options the serialisation is exactly as before: every loaded relationship, unlimited depth. `seen` (NTS-597) tracks the entities on the current serialisation path — a graph that re-reaches one of its own ancestors (a cycle) throws a NeodeError instead of overflowing the stack. Shared (non-cyclic) sub-graphs serialise in full.
- `TransactionalService` (class) — The INeode surface scoped to one open transaction: every read/write runs through the TransactionHandle opened by `Neode#beginTransaction` until its commit/rollback, with the facade's model methods (create, merge, relate, …) mirrored inside that scope. The close endpoints are safe to sequence: a second commit() is a no-op and a rollback after a commit does nothing (the managed scopes commit on success), while a commit after a rollback throws.
- `TransactionError` (class) — Thrown by Neode.batch() when any statement of the batch fails and the transaction is rolled back (port of neode's TransactionError): - `errors` — per-statement error aligned with the input batch, null where the statement succeeded - `results` — results of the statements that succeeded before the failure - `details` — the failed statements only ({ index, query, params, error })
- `TransactionHandle` (interface) — An explicit transaction: statements run in scope until commit/rollback.
- `valueToJson` (function) — Convert a single property value into its JSON friendly shape.
- `WhereNull` (class) — An `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` predicate on a property, rendered by toString() — the value of `Builder.whereNull` / `whereNotNull`.
- `withFilterParams` (function) — Run the work with request-scoped filter params (NTS-575). Every read the work performs — across awaits, and isolated from concurrent callers — sees these values, which take precedence over `setFilterParams` defaults. Scopes nest: an inner scope overrides the outer one name by name, and a value of `undefined` hides the outer/default value inside the scope. `ts await withFilterParams({ tenant: req.tenantId }, async () => { await Article.all() }) ` Needs a runtime with AsyncLocalStorage (Node.js), like ambient transactions.
- `WITHOUT_ALL_FILTERS` (const) — The reserved withoutFilters entry that disables EVERY named filter for the query — the write paths' internal re-hydration (save / create / merge use FindByIdService to re-read the row they just wrote) must find rows the current filter view hides. Filters are a read policy; writes never read through them.

## kNN & full-text search

```ts
import { knn, search, toFulltextQuery } from 'neode'

const vectorHits = await knn(runner, 'Person', 'person_plot_vector', vector, 5)
const textHits = await search(runner, 'Person', 'person_plot', toFulltextQuery(query))
```

### Search API

- `search` (function) — Full-text search over a full-text index (`CALL db.index.fulltext.queryNodes`), returning hydrated entities with their relevance score, best match first. The query string is bound as a parameter, so Lucene syntax characters in it are still parsed as such — pass user text through `toFulltextQuery` first. NTS-162 — the model's named read filters apply (a `WHERE` after the YIELD); `filters.withoutFilters` disables names for this call.
- `knn` (function) — k-nearest-neighbour search over a vector index, returning hydrated entities with their similarity score, best match first. With the default `auto` mode the Cypher 25 `SEARCH` clause is attempted first and the queryNodes procedure is used as a fallback; when the backend supports neither a combined error is raised. NTS-162 — the model's named read filters apply to both query forms (a `WHERE` over the matched / YIELDed rows); `filters.withoutFilters` disables names for this call. NTS-584 — the filters are a post-filter over the index's top-k: the SEARCH clause's in-index `WHERE` only takes property predicates over properties registered as additional filter properties on the vector index (which neode's index definitions never declare) and has no label predicates, so the soft-delete filter can never go there. Filtered searches therefore over-fetch round over round until k rows survive the filters or the round cap gives up — k is filled whenever that many valid neighbours exist.
- `toFulltextQuery` (function) — Sanitise free user text into a safe full-text query string: Lucene syntax characters and uppercase boolean operators stripped, terms lowercased and capped at `maxTerms` (default 12). Pass user text through this before `search()` / `Repository#search` — binding the string as a parameter stops Cypher injection, but the Lucene parser still 500s on syntax characters (`(`, `"`, `*`, `AND`, …).
- `FulltextIndexService` (class) — Installs/drops the given full-text index definitions, following the same result-reporting pattern as SchemaService
- `VectorIndexService` (class) — Installs/drops the given vector index definitions, following the same result-reporting pattern as SchemaService

## Testing

```ts
import { wipe, testId } from 'neode'

await wipe(neode, { confirm: true }) // DESTRUCTIVE: drop every constraint + all data (local test DBs only)
const name = testId('person') // unique per-run ids, safe for parallel suites
```

### Testing & ops API

- `ConnectivityConfig` (interface) — The connection config the checks run against — the shape fromEnv() produces (uri + auth + driver config + database).
- `ConnectivityTimeoutError` (class) — Rejected by waitUntilReachable when the deadline passes.
- `FactoryBuilder` (class) — Chainable factory builder (NTS-444): seed fake data through the library's normal create/relate services, so validation, defaults, timestamps and relationship logic all apply. neode.factory('User') .count(10) .with('posts', { count: 2, properties: { title: 'Seeded' } }) .create({ role: 'admin' }) Precedence on create: explicit value > `default` > `fake`. Unique properties with a `fake` generator are retried until the values are distinct within one batch (app-level check) — across runs the user's fake fn must be DB-safe (e.g. random UUIDs). An override on a unique property applies to the first row; later rows fake distinct values around it. `.make()` resolves the same properties but returns unsaved instances; `.has(otherFactory, relationshipName)` composes another factory's output onto every created instance through the explicit relate path.
- `FactoryWithSpec` (interface) — Options for one `.with()` call on a factory builder (NTS-444)
- `runCypherScript` (function) — Run every statement of a script sequentially against a runner. Stops at (rejects on) the first failing statement.
- `RunCypherScriptOptions` (interface) — Options for runCypherScript.
- `runSeeders` (function) — Run seeders in order against one Neode instance.
- `seededRandom` (function) — A deterministic PRNG (mulberry32) for reproducible fixtures (NTS-167): seed it once and use it inside property `fake` generators — the same seed produces the same sequence, so seeded fixtures stay stable across runs. const random = seededRandom(42)
- `Seeder` (class) — Base class for seeders (NTS-167): `runSeeders()` calls seed() once per seeder, in order. Write idempotently inside seed() — `neode.mergeOn(model, match, set)` or `neode.merge(model, properties)` MERGE on the node's merge fields — so rerunning the runner updates instead of duplicating.
- `splitCypherStatements` (function) — Split a script's contents into statements. Semicolons split statements except when they appear inside: - single- or double-quoted string literals (backslash escapes honoured), - backtick-quoted identifiers (`` `a``b` `` doubling honoured), - `--`and`//`line comments, and`/*` block comments (to the closer). Chunks that hold nothing but whitespace and comments are dropped, and each remaining statement is trimmed. Comments that belong to a statement are kept — they are legal Cypher.
- `testId` (function) — Unique identifier for test data — `test-<timestamp>-<random>` by default, safe as a property value (letters, digits and hyphens only).
- `verifyConnectivity` (function) — Check that a database is reachable right now, using a throwaway driver constructed from the config (closed again afterwards). Note the check runs with whatever connectionTimeout the config carries — the driver's default applies otherwise.
- `waitUntilReachable` (function) — Retry verifyConnectivity with exponential-ish backoff until the database is reachable or the timeout elapses (then: ConnectivityTimeoutError).
- `WaitUntilReachableOptions` (interface) — Backoff and probe options for waitUntilReachable — every field optional.
- `wipe` (function) — Wipe the database clean for a test run: DETACH DELETE every node (batched, `CALL { } IN TRANSACTIONS` where supported), reset the graph type to empty (NTS-550 — graph-type-derived constraints only go with the type; Enterprise servers only), then drop every constraint and index the database currently has. DESTRUCTIVE (NTS-578): this destroys whatever database the runner points at, so it refuses to run without `{ confirm: true }` (or `NEODE_ALLOW_WIPE=true`), refuses a non-local `uri` (or `NEO4J_URI`) unless `allowRemote: true`, and verifies the connected database name when `database` is given. Never point it at a shared database. Standalone on purpose — SchemaService derives DROP statements from the registered models, while wipe() discovers them from the database itself (small duplication of its statement shapes, accepted). Only "unsupported syntax" errors are tolerated (graph types on Community / pre-2026.02 servers); everything else — authentication, permissions, connectivity — is thrown. Constraint and index drops that fail are listed in the returned report's `failed` instead of being swallowed; built-in lookup indexes are skipped.
- `WipeReport` (interface) — What wipe() did. Returned instead of `void` (NTS-578): awaiting wipe() and ignoring the result keeps working.
- `WipeTarget` (type) — A Runner, or any facade exposing one (e.g. Neode — matched structurally to avoid importing the service here).

## Errors

### Error taxonomy

- `CardinalityViolationError` (class) — Raised when a write would give a relationship more edges than its declared cardinality allows (NTS-161): relating a second edge onto a `one` / `zeroOrOne` relationship — through relate(), a multi-target save, or syncEdges — names the relationship, the violated cardinality and the fix. Detach the existing edge first (or use syncEdges, which detaches for you), or change the declaration to `many`.
- `classifyError` (function) — Map a raw driver/engine error to the typed taxonomy (NTS-129): constraint violations → ConstraintViolationError, transient codes and retryable-flagged failures → TransientError. Everything else — unknown shapes and already-typed errors — passes through untouched.
- `ConstraintViolationError` (class) — A unique-constraint violation, raised on `merge()`/`create()` flows that race an existing node. `label`/`property` are parsed from the database message when it names them (Neo4j does; the embedded Relate engine only names the constraint), and stay undefined otherwise.
- `isTransientError` (function) — Type guard for classified transient errors.
- `NeodeError` (class) — Base class of the typed error taxonomy (NTS-129). Typed errors are produced by `classifyError`, which wraps the raw driver/engine error — the original is preserved as `cause`. House rule (NTS-442): every error names what failed, where, why, and suggests the fix — `<what failed> in <where> — <why>. <suggested fix>`. Driver failures carry the failing statement with REDACTED parameters (`redactParameters` — keys and shapes, never values).
- `OptimisticLockError` (class) — Raised when an optimistic-lock check (NTS-158) matched zero rows: the `@Version` property the instance was hydrated with no longer matches the stored one — the node was modified or deleted by another transaction. This is NOT a transient failure: retrying without reloading will fail again. Reload the entity (find / findById / a fresh get) and re-apply the change. The stable `name` lets retry helpers exclude it from transient- retry classification.
- `RelationNotLoadedError` (class) — Raised when strict relation access is on (setStrictRelationAccess) and a relationship property the load spec did not request is read off a hydrated entity (NTS-155). The message names the exact fix: request the relation in the load spec (`with`) or load it on the instance.
- `TransientError` (class) — A transient failure (`Neo.TransientError.*` codes, or the driver's / engine's own `retryable` verdict): retrying the operation may succeed. `isRetryable` is baked in by the code classification — a TransientError is only ever created for a retryable failure.

## Agent ontology API

Emit the live graph schema for grounding Text2Cypher prompts or MCP resources:

```ts
import { ontology, ontologyMarkdown } from 'neode'

// Ground a Text2Cypher prompt: hand the LLM the live schema, not its
// training-data memory of it.
const systemPrompt = [
  'You write Cypher against the graph described below.',
  'Only use the entities, properties and relationships listed.',
  '',
  ontologyMarkdown(),
].join('\n')

// Or expose it over MCP as a resource / tool result:
server.resource('graph-ontology', () => ontologyMarkdown())
server.tool('describe-ontology', async () => ({
  content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify(ontology()) }],
}))
```
